tagline: Turn Linear issues assigned to you into personal Todoist tasks automatically
metaTitle: Linear + Todoist Integration: Linear Assignments in Todoist
metaDescription: Turn Linear assignments into Todoist tasks and sync completion back to Linear. GAIA keeps your personal list current. See the setup steps.
intro:
Most engineers manage their work in at least two places: the team issue tracker and their personal task manager. Linear drives the sprint; Todoist (or a notebook, or a whiteboard) drives the individual. Keeping both aligned manually is friction that adds up — copying issue titles, tracking due dates in two places, remembering to mark things done in both systems.

GAIA eliminates that duplication by watching for assignments and automatically creating corresponding tasks in your Todoist. When an issue is assigned to you, it appears there with the right project, priority, and due date. When you complete it in either tool, GAIA marks it done in the other. Your personal task list reflects your real engineering workload without any manual copying.

This integration is ideal for engineers who use their task manager as the single place for all tasks — personal errands, recurring work, and engineering tickets — and want Linear to feed into that system automatically rather than competing with it.

useCases.title: Auto-create Todoist tasks from Linear assignments
useCases.description: Every time an issue is assigned to you, GAIA creates a matching task with the issue title, Linear URL, priority, and target date so your personal task list is always current without any manual entry.

useCases.title: Sync task completion back to Linear
useCases.description: When you check off a task in Todoist, GAIA marks the linked issue as completed so your team's board stays accurate even if you prefer to track your own work there.

useCases.title: Organize issues by project in Todoist
useCases.description: GAIA maps teams and projects to their counterpart projects so engineering work lands in the right section of your task list and doesn't get mixed up with unrelated personal tasks.

useCases.title: Morning digest of today's priorities
useCases.description: Each morning GAIA checks your queue for high-priority issues due today or overdue and adds a task reminding you to review and action them before daily standup.

useCases.title: Flag overdue issues in your task list
useCases.description: When an issue's due date passes without resolution, GAIA creates an urgent task flagging it so it surfaces in your personal productivity system and doesn't get buried on the team board.

howItWorks.step: Connect Linear and Todoist to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your accounts for both tools. GAIA identifies which Linear user you are and maps your assignments to your Todoist inbox.

howItWorks.step: Configure project mapping and sync preferences
howItWorks.description: Choose which teams or projects should feed your task list, which project each should map to, and whether completions should sync bidirectionally.
GAIA monitors your assignments and keeps the task list updated automatically. You can triage your day there while teammates see accurate status on the team board.

faqs.question: Will GAIA create a Todoist task for every Linear issue in the workspace or only my assignments?
faqs.answer: By default GAIA only creates tasks for issues assigned to your user. You can optionally configure it to also watch issues you've subscribed to or issues in a specific team regardless of assignment.

faqs.question: What happens when an issue is reassigned away from me?
faqs.answer: GAIA detects the reassignment and marks the corresponding task as cancelled or deletes it, depending on your preference. This prevents stale tasks from cluttering your personal list.

faqs.question: Can I edit the task without affecting the issue?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can freely edit the task title, add subtasks, set reminders, or move it to a different project without those changes touching the issue. Only task completion is synced back; everything else is yours to manage locally.
